Q: git: How to delete a local ref branch? A:

Just do

git branch -d commits

to delete the local branch.

Use the -d switch to delete it irrespective of its merged status.

Use

git update-ref -d refs/notes/origin/commits

to delete the ref.

You can also hard-delete it as mentioned in other answers with

rm -rf .git/refs/notes

Q: on click on element, react fails with "destroy is not a function" A:

Chrome recently updated the scrollToView function to return a Promise, as already updated in the spec. Previously, the result was falsy.

With this, useEffect thinks that the returned promise is its cleanup function, tries to call it, and BOOM 💥.

Q: Why is the commit necessary to handle the DateTime data correctly? A:

In general, SQLAlchemy doesn't perform any conversion or coercion on the values set for column attributes. Rather, it passes the values as-is to the driver (for example, psycopg2) to construct an insert or update statement. If a DateTime attribute is set to a string value then accessing the attribute will return a string.

However, when a session is committed, any model instances in the session are expired*, which erases their attribute values. The next time that an attribute is accessed the database is queried to fetch its value. The type of the value will now be of the expected type. A similar effect is obtained by refreshing the instance.

So in short, if you want the attribute to be a datetime instance before committing you need to convert it yourself or manually flush the session.

* Unless the session has expire_on_commit set to False.
